index.lead: How Veilus fits e-commerce, dropshipping, affiliate marketing, advertising and web scraping, and how to keep accounts on each platform in their own profiles — for accounts you own or are authorized to manage.

benefits.title: One profile per {unit}
benefits.body: Each {unit} lives in its own profile with its own cookies, site storage, fingerprint and proxy. Profiles don't share browser data, so all your {platform} {units} stay signed in at once — no logging out and back in.

benefits.title: Your other computers, through Veilus Sync
benefits.body: On a paid plan, Veilus Sync copies profiles — settings, cookies and site storage — between computers through a Git repository or Google Drive you own. Syncing is manual, and Veilus has no per-user roles. Profile data is uploaded as-is, so use a private repository.

benefits.title: Repetitive work, automated
benefits.body: On a paid plan, Veilus Flow runs Playwright scripts on your profiles, in batches or on a schedule. Write a script yourself, or let an AI assistant write and fix it over MCP; scripts added over MCP or the REST API run on at most 3 profiles until you approve them in the app.
benefits.linkText: MCP, local API and SDK for developers

steps.title: Download and create profiles
steps.body: Install Veilus on Windows 10/11 (x64) or macOS 13.5+ (Apple Silicon). Create one profile per {unit} and set its language, timezone and proxy.

steps.title: Sign in once in each profile
steps.body: Open each profile and sign in to its {platform} {unit}. The session stays in that profile between launches.

steps.title: Automate or schedule
steps.body: Approve a script in Veilus Flow, then run it on the profiles as a batch or put it on a schedule. This needs a paid plan or the 7-day Pro trial.

ecommerce.name: e-commerce
ecommerce.metaTitle: Veilus for e-commerce — one browser profile per store, storefront checks per market
ecommerce.metaDescription: Keep each store you run in its own Veilus profile, check storefronts, prices and listings in each market's language and timezone, and run the checks on a schedule.
ecommerce.sub: Keep each store you run in its own browser profile, on marketplaces and platforms that allow more than one store, and check your storefronts in every market's language and timezone.

benefits.title: One profile per store
benefits.body: Each store's admin lives in its own profile with its own cookies, site storage, fingerprint and proxy, so every store stays signed in and you switch stores by switching windows.

benefits.title: Storefronts per market
benefits.body: Set each profile's browser language and timezone, or pick a market to fill both. A profile doesn't change your IP address: if a storefront picks language or currency from the IP, give the profile a proxy in that region.

benefits.title: Checks that run on their own
benefits.body: On a paid plan, an approved Playwright script reads what each profile gets — the page's language, prices, listing text — and prints it to Run History, in a batch or on a schedule. An AI assistant can write it for you over MCP.
benefits.linkText: MCP, local API and SDK for developers

steps.title: Create profiles for stores and markets
steps.body: Install Veilus on Windows 10/11 (x64) or macOS 13.5+ (Apple Silicon). Create one profile per store and one per market you check, each with its language, timezone and proxy.

steps.title: Sign in and tag
steps.body: Sign in to each store in its own profile. Tag the market profiles so a saved filter selects them together.

steps.title: Write one check and schedule it
steps.body: Ask an AI assistant over MCP to write the check, or write it yourself. Approve it in Veilus Flow and put it on a daily schedule: a page that shows the wrong language or price can fail its profile.

guides.text: Guide: check a site in several languages and time zones

faq.q: Can I run several stores on one marketplace?
faq.a: Only where the marketplace allows it. Some marketplaces allow more than one store per seller, some only with approval, and some not at all. Check its seller terms first; Veilus is for stores you run where that is allowed.

faq.q: How do I check prices and listings in another market?
faq.a: Create a profile with that market's language and timezone, and give it a proxy in the region if the site picks content from the visitor's IP. A script then opens the page in that profile and prints what it shows.

faq.q: Can the check run every day?
faq.a: Yes, on a paid plan. Put the approved script on a schedule. A script that exits with a non-zero code marks its profile as failed, and each profile's output and exit code show up in Run History.

faq.q: Where are store logins kept?
faq.a: In the profile: cookies and sessions stay there between launches. Account details that a script needs can go in a fixed dataset, where each profile gets its own row and no two profiles share one. Dataset values are stored on your computer in plain text.

faq.q: What does the Free plan cover?
faq.a: 5 profiles on 1 device, with no time limit and no card. Veilus Flow, schedules, batch runs, the local API/MCP, Veilus Sync and import/export need a paid plan; the app also has a 7-day Pro trial.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: Follow each marketplace's and platform's own terms, including any rule on how many stores a seller may have and on automated access, and use only stores you own or are authorized to manage. Our Acceptable Use Policy lists what Veilus may not be used for.

steps.title: Create profiles
steps.body: Install Veilus on Windows 10/11 (x64) or macOS 13.5+ (Apple Silicon). Create a profile per store and one per market you sell to, with its language, timezone and proxy.

faq.q: Can Veilus check supplier prices and stock for me?
faq.a: A script can, on a paid plan: it opens each supplier page, reads the values and prints them. Veilus keeps the last 4096 characters of each profile's output; for more, the script writes to a file and prints a short summary.

faq.q: Do supplier sites allow automated checks?
faq.a: That depends on the site. Check its terms and robots.txt first; some sites prohibit automated collection. Keep Concurrency low and wait between pages inside the script.

faq.q: Can I check my store in another country's language?
faq.a: Yes. Create a profile with that market's language and timezone. A profile doesn't change your IP address, so if your storefront picks language or currency from the IP, give the profile a proxy in that region.

faq.q: Do I need to write code?
faq.a: No. Describe the check to an AI assistant connected over MCP, such as Claude Code or Cursor. It writes the Playwright script and trial-runs it on up to 3 profiles; you read it and approve it before it runs on more.

faq.q: Can I keep several stores signed in at once?
faq.a: Yes. Sign in to each store in its own profile. Each profile keeps its own cookies and site storage between launches, so you switch stores by switching windows.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: Follow the terms of each platform you sell on and of each supplier site you check, and use only stores you own or are authorized to manage. Our Acceptable Use Policy lists what Veilus may not be used for.

affiliate-marketing.name: affiliate marketing
affiliate-marketing.metaTitle: Veilus for affiliate marketing — check your links and landing pages per country
affiliate-marketing.metaDescription: Keep your own affiliate sites and network accounts in separate Veilus profiles, check that your own landing pages and redirects show the right content per country and language, and monitor public offer pages on a schedule.
affiliate-marketing.sub: Keep your own sites and network accounts in separate browser profiles, and check that your own landing pages and redirects show the right content in each country and language.

benefits.title: Your accounts, kept apart
benefits.body: Each of your affiliate network accounts and site dashboards lives in its own profile with its own cookies and site storage, so they all stay signed in at once.

benefits.title: Your pages checked per country and language
benefits.body: A profile carries its own browser language and timezone, and a proxy in a region shows what a browser there gets. A script opens each of your own landing pages and redirects and prints where it lands and which language the page declares.

benefits.title: Public pages monitored on a schedule
benefits.body: On a paid plan, an approved script checks your own landing pages and public offer pages on a schedule, and a page that breaks shows up as a failed profile.
benefits.linkText: MCP, local API and SDK for developers

steps.title: Create profiles
steps.body: Install Veilus on Windows 10/11 (x64) or macOS 13.5+ (Apple Silicon). Create one profile per account you own, and one per country you check, with its language, timezone and a proxy in that region.

steps.title: List your own pages
steps.body: Give the script the URLs of your own landing pages and redirects as a variable, so every country profile checks the same list.

steps.title: Approve and schedule
steps.body: Ask an AI assistant over MCP to write the check, or write it yourself. Approve it in Veilus Flow, put it on a schedule and read each profile's result in Run History.

faq.q: Can I use several accounts on one affiliate network?
faq.a: Only if the network's terms allow it. Veilus is not for extra accounts that get around a network's limits, fake clicks or traffic, cookie stuffing or paid fake sign-ups: those break our Acceptable Use Policy.

faq.q: How do I check a landing page from another country?
faq.a: Create a profile with that country's language and timezone and a proxy in the region. A script opens your page in that profile and prints the final URL and the language the page declares.

faq.q: Can the checks run on a schedule?
faq.a: Yes, on a paid plan. Point the checks at your own pages and redirects, not at network tracking links, so automated visits are never counted as clicks; check your network's terms.

faq.q: Where do I see the results?
faq.a: In the script's Run History: each profile's output and exit code. An AI assistant connected over MCP can read the same results and tell you which pages failed.

faq.q: Will networks detect my profiles?
faq.a: No tool can promise that, and we don't. Each profile keeps its own fingerprint, proxy and cookies; how your accounts are treated also depends on how you use them.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: Follow the terms of each affiliate network and platform you work with, and use only sites and accounts you own or are authorized to manage. Our Acceptable Use Policy lists what Veilus may not be used for.

steps.title: Create profiles
steps.body: Install Veilus on Windows 10/11 (x64) or macOS 13.5+ (Apple Silicon). Create one profile per client account and one per region you check, each with its language, timezone and proxy.

steps.title: Sign in with permission
steps.body: Sign in to each client account you are authorized to manage in its own profile, and tag the profiles by client.

steps.title: Automate the checks
steps.body: Approve a script in Veilus Flow, run it as a batch or on a schedule, and read each profile's output in Run History.

faq.q: Can I see my ad the way people in another country do?
faq.a: A profile with that market's language and timezone, and a proxy in the region, shows what a browser there gets. What an ad platform chooses to show also depends on its own targeting, so treat it as a check, not a guarantee.

faq.q: We manage ad accounts for clients. How do we keep them apart?
faq.a: Give each client account you are authorized to manage its own profile, name it after the account and tag it by client. Profiles don't share browser data, so each client's session stays in that client's profile.

faq.q: Can I automate reporting checks?
faq.a: Yes, on a paid plan: an approved Playwright script runs on the profiles as a batch or on a schedule. Check each ad platform's terms on automated access before you automate anything there.

faq.q: Can a teammate open the same client profiles?
faq.a: With Veilus Sync on a paid plan, profiles, cookies included, are copied between computers through a Git repository or Google Drive you own; keep it private. Syncing is manual, and Veilus has no per-user roles.

faq.q: Can Veilus help after an ad account is suspended?
faq.a: No. Running ads again after a ban, getting around an ad platform's review, or creating replacement accounts is against our Acceptable Use Policy. Follow the platform's own process.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: Follow each ad platform's own terms and policies, and use only accounts you own or are authorized to manage. Our Acceptable Use Policy lists what Veilus may not be used for.

benefits.title: Scripts in a real profile
benefits.body: A Veilus Flow script runs inside a profile's browser, so each request goes out with that profile's fingerprint, proxy and cookies, and logins stay in the profile between runs.

faq.q: Do I need to write code?
faq.a: No. Describe what to collect to an AI assistant connected over MCP, such as Claude Code or Cursor. It writes the Playwright script and trial-runs it on up to 3 profiles; you read it and approve it before it runs on more.

faq.q: How much output does a run keep?
faq.a: Veilus keeps the last 4096 characters of each profile's output. If you collect more, have the script write it to a file with Node's fs module and print a short summary.

faq.q: Do trial runs get dataset rows?
faq.a: No. Dataset values reach approved scripts only; a trial run of an unapproved script gets none and reserves no rows. Pass the values it needs as run variables instead.

faq.q: Can a profile keep its login between runs?
faq.a: Yes. Cookies and logins stay in the profile, so reuse the same profile for the same site and its session carries over from run to run.

faq.q: Will sites block my scripts?
faq.a: No tool can promise that, and we don't. A profile keeps a consistent fingerprint, proxy and cookies; how a site treats the traffic also depends on how fast and how much you collect.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: It depends on the site and where you are. Check each site's terms and robots.txt before you collect from it; some sites prohibit automated collection. Collect public data, keep the pace low, and read our Acceptable Use Policy.

instagram.name: Instagram
instagram.metaTitle: Manage multiple Instagram accounts — one browser profile each | Veilus
instagram.metaDescription: Keep your brand, personal and client Instagram accounts each in its own Veilus browser profile with its own cookies, fingerprint and proxy, all signed in at once.
instagram.sub: Keep your brand, personal and client Instagram accounts each in its own browser profile, all signed in at once.

faq.q: Can I keep my brand account and my personal account open at the same time?
faq.a: Yes. Put each one in its own profile. Each profile has its own cookies and site storage, so both stay signed in and you switch accounts by switching windows, not by logging out.

faq.q: I manage Instagram for clients. How do I keep their accounts apart?
faq.a: Give each client account you are authorized to manage its own profile, name the profile after the account and tag it by client. Profiles don't share browser data, so each client's session stays in that client's profile.

faq.q: Do I need a proxy for every account?
faq.a: Veilus doesn't require one. If you want a profile to go out through its own connection, give it an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy. Before every launch, Veilus checks that the profile's timezone matches where the proxy exits.

faq.q: Can a colleague open the same accounts on their computer?
faq.a: With Veilus Sync on a paid plan, profiles, cookies included, are copied between computers through a Git repository or Google Drive you own. Syncing is manual, and the same profile shouldn't be open on two computers at once. Veilus has no per-user roles or permissions.

faq.q: Will Instagram detect my profiles?
faq.a: No tool can promise that, and we don't. Each profile keeps its own fingerprint, proxy and cookies; how your accounts are treated also depends on how you use them.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: Follow Instagram's own rules, including any limit on how many accounts you may have and what it says about automated activity, and use only accounts you own or are authorized to manage. Check Instagram's terms before you start. Our Acceptable Use Policy lists what Veilus may not be used for.

tiktok.name: TikTok
tiktok.metaTitle: Manage multiple TikTok accounts — one browser profile each | Veilus
tiktok.metaDescription: Run separate brand and regional TikTok accounts from one computer, each in its own Veilus profile with its own language, timezone, cookies and proxy.
tiktok.sub: Run separate brand and regional TikTok accounts from one computer, each in its own profile with its own language, timezone and proxy.

faq.q: We run a separate TikTok account for each region. Can each profile match its region?
faq.a: Yes. When you create a profile you set its browser language and timezone, or pick a market to fill both. A Config check flags a language that doesn't match the timezone. A profile doesn't change your IP address; for that, give it a proxy in the region.

faq.q: Can I keep several brand accounts signed in at once?
faq.a: Yes. Put each account in its own profile. Each profile keeps its own cookies and site storage between launches, so every account stays signed in and you never log one out to open another.

faq.q: Why won't a profile open?
faq.a: Before every launch, Veilus compares the profile's timezone with where its proxy, or your own network, exits, and by default blocks a launch that doesn't match. With a proxy pool selected, use Match to proxy in the profile's Network tab; otherwise change the profile's timezone, or set Settings → Timezone check to Warn or Off.

faq.q: Can I automate routine work across the accounts?
faq.a: On a paid plan, Veilus Flow runs Playwright scripts on many profiles at once or on a schedule, and an AI assistant connected over MCP can write them. Read TikTok's terms on automated activity before you automate anything there.

faq.q: Will TikTok detect my profiles?
faq.a: No tool can promise that, and we don't. Each profile keeps its own fingerprint, proxy and cookies; how your accounts are treated also depends on how you use them.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: Follow TikTok's own rules, including any limit on how many accounts you may have and what it says about automated activity, and use only accounts you own or are authorized to manage. Check TikTok's terms before you start. Our Acceptable Use Policy lists what Veilus may not be used for.

youtube.name: YouTube
youtube.metaTitle: Manage multiple YouTube accounts and channels — one browser profile each | Veilus
youtube.metaDescription: Keep the Google account behind each of your YouTube channels in its own Veilus browser profile with its own cookies, fingerprint and proxy, all signed in at once.
youtube.sub: Keep the Google account behind each of your channels in its own browser profile, all signed in at once.

faq.q: Do I need a separate profile for each channel?
faq.a: A profile holds whatever Google account you sign in to in it, so profiles separate accounts, not channels. Separate profiles help when your channels belong to different Google accounts and you want them all signed in at once.

faq.q: Can I stay signed in to several Google accounts at the same time?
faq.a: Yes. Sign in to one account per profile. Each profile has its own cookies and site storage, so the sessions don't mix and each one is still there the next time you open the profile.

faq.q: Can my editor work on a channel from another computer?
faq.a: With Veilus Sync on a paid plan, a profile is copied, cookies included, through a Git repository or Google Drive you own. That copy carries the live sign-in, so anyone who can read the repository can use the session: keep it private. Veilus has no per-user roles.

faq.q: Can I run the same routine on every channel?
faq.a: On a paid plan, yes. An approved Playwright script runs on each profile as a batch or on a schedule, and each profile's output and exit code show up in Run History. Check YouTube's terms on automated activity first.

faq.q: Will YouTube detect my profiles?
faq.a: No tool can promise that, and we don't. Each profile keeps its own fingerprint, proxy and cookies; how your accounts are treated also depends on how you use them.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: Follow YouTube's and Google's own rules, including what they say about multiple accounts and automated activity, and use only accounts you own or are authorized to manage. Check their terms before you start. Our Acceptable Use Policy lists what Veilus may not be used for.

x.metaTitle: Manage multiple X (Twitter) accounts — one browser profile each | Veilus

x.sub: Keep the X accounts for your different projects each in its own browser profile, all signed in at once.

faq.q: I run X accounts for several projects. How do I keep them apart?
faq.a: Give each account its own profile, name it after the account and tag it by project. Save a filter by tag, and a schedule can run on that filter, so profiles you tag later are picked up.

faq.q: Can each account use its own proxy?
faq.a: Yes. Each profile can have its own HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy. With a static proxy pool set to 1:1 Dedicated, each profile gets its own proxy from the pool.

faq.q: Can I automate repetitive work on X?
faq.a: On a paid plan, Veilus Flow runs Playwright scripts on your profiles in batches or on a schedule. Check X's terms on automation first and keep any script within them.

faq.q: How do I move an account's profile to another computer?
faq.a: On a paid plan, export the profile to a .veiluspack file and import it on the other computer, or use Veilus Sync to copy profiles through a Git repository or Google Drive you own. Don't open the same profile on two computers at once.

faq.q: Will X detect my profiles?
faq.a: No tool can promise that, and we don't. Each profile keeps its own fingerprint, proxy and cookies; how your accounts are treated also depends on how you use them.

faq.q: Is this allowed?
faq.a: Follow X's own rules, including what they say about running more than one account and about automation, and use only accounts you own or are authorized to manage. Check X's terms before you start. Our Acceptable Use Policy lists what Veilus may not be used for.
